 3   Q.      Please state your name and business address.

 4   A.      My name is Allison M. Johnson. My business address is 3500 Blake Street, Denver,

 7   A.      I am filing testimony on behalf of Southwestern Public Service Company, a New

 1                 II.   BENCH REQUEST QUESTIONS ADDRESSED IN THIS
 2                               SUPPLEMENTAL TESTIMONY

 3                            QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(c):

 4   Q.   What is the amount of executive compensation, by position, that SPS seeks to

 5        recover in its cost of service?

 6   A.   SPS calculates its revenue requirement using aggregated labor expense recorded by

 7        functional area and Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”) account as

 8        required by the FERC Uniform System of Accounts (“USoA”). As a result, SPS’s

 9        accounting and cost-of-service models do not track compensation at the individual

10        employee level, therefore SPS cannot identify the exact amount of executive

11        compensation, by position, within the cost of service. Attachment AMJ-BR 1(c)

12        provides an approximate annual amount of executive compensation occurring

13        within the calendar years that the period July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2025 (“Base

14        Period”) cost of service includes.

15               The methodology used to escalate Base Period labor to the period December

16        1, 2026, through November 30, 2027 (“Future Test Year Period”) was consistent

17        with prior practices in previous SPS base rate proceedings and the development of

18        SPS cost of service studies. This is discussed in detail in the Direct Testimony of

19        SPS witness Tamra Newman. The Future Test Year period executive compensation


                                               3
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                  Supplemental Testimony
                                             of
                                    Allison M. Johnson

 1        follows these practices. As discussed by Ms. Newman; Non-bargaining wages

 2        (base pay) were escalated based on a 3.0 percent increase for both 2026 and 2027,

3         Annual Incentive Plan (“AIP”) expense reflects expenses incurred during the Base

4         Period and two 3.0 percent market-based increases to the base pay of AIP-eligible

 5        employees      representing    target-level    payouts,    and     LTI     equals

 6        the requested performance LTI and time-based LTI actually incurred during the

 7        Base Period.

 8                            QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(e):

 9   Q.   What is SPS's requested non-fuel revenue requirement in this case?

10   A.   Please refer to Attachment AMJ-BR 1(e), page 2, line no. 15, filed as Attachment

11        AMJ-5 to the Direct Testimony of Allison M. Johnson. SPS’s proposed non-fuel

12        revenue requirement is $892,652,373.

13                            QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(h):

14   Q.   If SPS were to collect all of its fuel costs through base rates, what would be the

15        base cost of fuel incorporated into new rates taking effect on January 1, 2027

16        (or whenever the proposed rates become effective)?

17   A.   Please refer to Attachment AMJ-BR 1(h), which is Schedule H-3 in SPS’s

18        Application for the requested information. SPS’s fuel costs are recovered through



                                              4
                                      Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                    Supplemental Testimony
                                               of
                                      Allison M. Johnson

 1        its Fuel and Purchased Power Cost Adjustment Clause (“FPPCAC”) mechanism.

 2        SPS’s FPPCAC was reviewed in its recent FPPCAC Continuation application, Case

 3        No. 24-00270-UT, and approved for continued use for four years. SPS is not

 4        proposing in this proceeding to change its methodology for collecting fuel costs to

 5        collect its fuel costs through base rates. SPS has provided in its initial application

6         (as required) a schedule forecasting New Mexico retail’s portion of system fuel and

7         purchased power costs for the Test Year (December 2026 through November

8         2027).

 9   Q.   Does this conclude your pre-filed supplemental testimony?

10   A.   Yes.
